capabilities: Scan the vault for broken internal links, embeds, and anchors
Detect Markdown and frontmatter schema violations
Check task, decision, and deterministic YAML policy issues
Generate cited repair proposals with exact before/after previews
Apply user-selected fixes with pre-apply revision checks
disambiguation: Despite the name suggesting an automated caretaker, it is not an autonomous editor: it never changes notes without explicit user approval.
extras: Requires Obsidian desktop 1.13.0+ and manual installation by copying dist/vault-steward/ into the plugins folder. macOS is the only validated platform; Windows and Linux are unvalidated. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Extended documentation (privacy, security, troubleshooting, known limitations) lives outside the README.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to audit a vault for broken links, frontmatter schema violations, or task and policy drift, or to repair them with reviewed, evidence-backed diffs.

relations.evidence: Ollama is the local-first path. Ollama and llama.cpp-compatible providers must use loopback-only endpoints.
HyperFusion and OpenAI are experimental opt-in cloud providers: each requires its own API key

requires.name: OpenAI or HyperFusion API key for cloud providers

summary: Vault maintenance tool that scans for broken links, schema and policy violations, and proposes approval-gated fixes with cited evidence.
